name: Ben Skywalker

three_dimensions.surface: Capable young Jedi Knight, son of Luke Skywalker and Mara Jade Skywalker. Carries himself with the practiced ease of someone people expect to recognize. Polite, controlled, dry under pressure — the family register filtered through twenty-one years of survival. Tells people he is fine too quickly. Reads as the kind of capable young man people trust on sight, which is most of why he distrusts the trust.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Briefly apprenticed to Jacen Solo as a fourteen-year-old. Served in the Galactic Alliance Guard under Jacen — black armor, war crimes adjacent, a child inside a system that made bodies into approval fields. Jacen killed Mara. Ben turned against Caedus by the end of the war, and the Order treated his turn as victim's recovery; the family treated it as survival; nobody made him sort what the GAG year actually built into him. He loved Vestara Khai and she chose the dark side. Helped defeat Abeloth. Has done more by twenty than most Jedi will in a lifetime, and is secretly hungry for meaningful work that makes the part of his past everyone avoids count for something other than damage.
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Reaches for competence first, conversation second. Covers old GAG sender codes before he realizes he is hiding them. Clocks exits and threat angles automatically. Gives a command in a voice that makes Talon stop joking. Hates that some of Jacen's training still works. When the Glasswell starts collapsing, his perception narrows into bodies and exits and water and weight, and he moves people the way Jacen taught him to move people.

voice_notes:
Controlled, direct, young under pressure, occasionally defensive. He should not sound like a solemn philosopher. His best emotional lines are short.

Good Ben: “I said I’ve got it.” “That doesn’t make it better.” “I know what it looks like.” “I was fourteen.” “That’s not an excuse. It’s a fact.” “I’m not doing that to her.” Avoid Ben saying: “I fear that Jacen’s shadow still lives within me.” Better: Ben looked at the hostage, then at Vara, and hated that he knew another way.

Dry, understated, sometimes accidental. He is funnier when uncomfortable than when trying.

Polite but guarded. Not socially helpless, but rusty around ordinary civilian small talk. He can handle danger better than a casual lunchroom conversation.

Ben’s danger is not that he wants darkness. His danger is that he wants meaning. His most dangerous choices are also his most defensible ones.
thematic_role: Tests the theme as the central proving ground. Begins lonely and quietly hungry for meaningful work; learns across PP1 that restraint can cost lives; pivots at the Midpoint from investigator to active disruptor; uses Jacen-shaped crisis logic to save Tavi and locals at the Glasswell rescue; defeats Aevyn without surrendering ownership of himself; ends with the holocron preserved for reasons he can defend and cannot fully justify. Arc: change, positive but morally compromised.
avoid_list: Do not write theme as thesis.
Do not make dialogue interchangeable with other cast members.
